label: Can be exposed by
summary: Whether the given character is able to expose the secret.
details: It runs on a secret and takes a character. Vanilla mostly passes the root character or the actor of the event.

label: Can be leased out
summary: Whether the title can be leased out to a holy order.
details: It runs on a title and takes `yes` or `no`. Vanilla only uses it with `yes`.

label: Could be parent of
summary: Whether the character was old enough to have had the given character as a child, judged at the time of that child's birth.
details: Only age is taken into account, nothing else such as traits or fertility. It runs on the possible parent and takes the child.

label: Can be tributary of
summary: Whether the character can become a tributary (a ruler who pays tribute) of the given character.
details: It runs on the would-be tributary and takes the would-be overlord. The game's documentation does not say which rules it checks.

label: Can own legend
summary: Whether the character can become the owner of the given legend.
details: It runs on a character and takes a legend. Vanilla passes a saved legend scope.

label: Benefits from artifact
summary: Whether the character gets the artifact's main bonuses.
details: It runs on a character and takes an artifact. Vanilla mostly passes `prev` (the previous scope in the chain), and sometimes a saved scope.

label: Can be cancelled
summary: Whether the travel plan can be cancelled.
details: The activity tied to the plan may forbid cancelling. It runs on a travel plan and takes `yes` or `no`. Vanilla always writes `yes`.

label: Can change aspiration
summary: Whether the dynasty house can change or upgrade its house aspiration.
details: It runs on a dynasty house and takes `yes` or `no`. Vanilla only uses `yes`.

label: Convertible to rite
summary: Whether characters can convert to the rite.
details: It runs on a rite. The game's documentation also refers to `set_can_convert_to_rite`. Vanilla only uses `yes`.

label: Can create faction
summary: Whether the character can create a faction of the given type against the given character.
details: It runs on the character who would found the faction. Vanilla uses it with claimant, independence and ceremonial claimant factions.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The kind of faction.
fields.values: a faction type, such as `claimant_faction` or `independence_faction`

fields.name: target
fields.text: The character the faction would act against.
fields.values: a character, such as `liege` or a saved scope

label: Can create men-at-arms
summary: Whether the character can create men-at-arms (professional soldiers) of the given type.
details: It runs on a character and takes a men-at-arms type key. The game's documentation says nothing more, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Can create task contract
summary: Whether the character can create a task contract of the given type, optionally for a given employer.
details: The documented example spells it `can_create_task_contact`, which is a typo in the game's documentation. Vanilla writes the block form with both fields.

fields.name: type_name
fields.text: The kind of task contract.

fields.name: employer
fields.text: The character who would be the employer.
fields.values: a character, usually a saved scope

label: Can create title men-at-arms
summary: Whether men-at-arms of the given type can be created for the title.
details: It runs on a title and takes a men-at-arms type key. The game's documentation says nothing more, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Can declare war
summary: Whether the character can declare war on the defender with the given casus belli (war reason) over the given titles.
details: It runs on the would-be attacker. The titles are the ones the war would target. A claimant can optionally be given too; the game's documentation does not say more about it.

fields.name: defender
fields.text: The character who would be attacked.

fields.name: casus_belli
fields.text: The war reason.

fields.name: target_titles
fields.text: The titles the war is for.
fields.values: a list of titles in braces

fields.name: claimant
fields.text: An optional claimant for the war.

label: Can disband army
summary: Whether the army can be disbanded.
details: It runs on an army and takes `yes` or `no`. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Can diverge culture
summary: Whether the ruler can diverge their culture, including whether they can pay the cost.
details: For a check that ignores the cost, use `can_diverge_excluding_cost`. It runs on a character and takes `yes` or `no`.

label: Can diverge, ignoring cost
summary: Whether the ruler can diverge their culture, without checking the cost.
details: `can_diverge` also checks the cost. It runs on a character and takes `yes` or `no`.

label: Can embrace tradition
summary: Whether the character can embrace a new cultural tradition.
details: Write just the tradition, or a block that also names an old tradition to replace. Vanilla almost always uses the block form with `tradition = prev`.

fields.name: tradition
fields.text: The new tradition to embrace.
fields.values: a tradition, such as `prev` or a saved scope

fields.name: replace
fields.text: An existing tradition that the new one would replace.

label: Can employ court position
summary: Whether the character can employ someone in the court position type, and the position is vacant.
details: It runs on the ruler and takes a court position type key. Vanilla uses it a lot, for positions such as court physician, bodyguard and champion.

label: Can enshrine artifact
summary: Whether the character can enshrine the artifact in the holy site.
details: It runs on a character. Vanilla gives the holy site and the artifact, both as scopes.

fields.name: holy_site
fields.text: The holy site that would hold the artifact.

fields.name: artifact
fields.text: The artifact to enshrine.

fields.name: slot
fields.text: Which slot of the holy site to use.

label: Can equip artifact
summary: Whether the character can equip the artifact.
details: It runs on a character and takes an artifact.

label: Can execute decision
summary: Whether the character can carry out the decision.
details: It runs on a character and takes a decision key. Vanilla mostly writes the key, but sometimes a scope.

label: Can fire councillor
summary: Whether the councillor holding this council task can be dismissed.
details: It checks the position's own firing rule and also rules such as the position being illegal to reassign. It runs on a council task and takes `yes` or `no`. The documented example writes `position_can_be_fired`, which differs from the key name, so use `can_fire_position` as vanilla does.

label: Can fund contribution
summary: Whether the character can pay for the given contribution to a great project.
details: The contribution must be a scope or saved variable. It checks the contribution's own conditions, and fails if the contribution is already funded or was locked because the project has started.

label: Can get innovation from
summary: Whether the culture can take an applicable innovation from the other culture.
details: The game's documentation says the innovation is picked at random from the other culture. It runs on a culture and takes the culture to learn from.

label: Can have children
summary: Whether nothing in the character, such as a trait, blocks them from having children.
details: It only checks hard blocks from traits, not fertility. It runs on a character and takes `yes` or `no`.

label: Can host activity
summary: Whether the character can host an activity of the given type.
details: It runs on a character and takes an activity type key, such as a feast or a pilgrimage.

label: Can hybridize
summary: Whether the ruler can hybridize their culture with the given culture, including whether they can pay the cost.
details: `can_hybridize_excluding_cost` skips the cost check.

label: Can hybridize, ignoring cost
summary: Whether the ruler can hybridize their culture with the given culture, without checking the cost.
details: `can_hybridize` also checks the cost. Vanilla does not use this key.

label: Can join activity
summary: Whether the character can join the given activity.
details: It runs on a character and takes an activity. Vanilla often passes a saved activity or a character's `involved_activity`.

label: Can join faction
summary: Whether the character can join the given faction.
details: It runs on a character and takes a faction. Vanilla often passes a saved faction or another character's `joined_faction`.

label: Can join or create faction against
summary: Whether the character can join or create a faction against the given character.
details: Write just the target character, or a block to narrow it to one faction type. By default it also checks whether the character is already in a faction. Set `check_in_a_faction = no` to skip that.

fields.name: who
fields.text: The character the faction would be against.

fields.name: faction
fields.text: Limits the check to this faction type.

fields.name: check_in_a_faction
fields.text: Whether to check if the character is already in a faction.

label: Can raze holding
summary: Whether the nomad can raze (destroy) the holding in the given province with the Raze Holding command.
details: The game's documentation calls it an interface trigger for the Raze Holding command. It runs on a character and takes a province.

label: Can pick personal tenet
summary: Whether the character can choose the given tenet (a core belief of a faith) as their personal tenet.
details: It runs on a character and takes a tenet key, such as `tenet_communion`.

label: Can plan great project
summary: Whether the character can start planning a great project of the given type somewhere in their realm.
details: It checks the project's `is_shown` and `can_start_planning` conditions and also whether the character can pay the cost. Vanilla writes the type either as a scope or as `great_project_type:key`.

label: Can plan project in province
summary: Whether the character can start planning the great project in the given province.
details: It fails if the planner or the project type is not valid. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: type_name
fields.text: The great project, by its key in the game's database.

fields.name: province
fields.text: The province for the project.

label: Can remove holy site artifact
summary: Whether the character can take the artifact out of the holy site.
details: It runs on a character. Vanilla gives the holy site and the artifact, both as scopes.

fields.name: holy_site
fields.text: The holy site that holds the artifact.

fields.name: artifact
fields.text: The artifact to remove.

label: Can sponsor inspiration
summary: Whether the character can sponsor the given inspiration.
details: It runs on the would-be sponsor and takes the inspiration.

label: Can start scheme
summary: Whether the character can start a scheme of the given type against the given target.
details: It runs on the character who would run the scheme. Vanilla names a target character for most types, and a target title for a few. The documented usage line writes `target`, but vanilla uses `target_character` and `target_title`.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The kind of scheme.
fields.values: a scheme type, such as `murder` or `seduce`

fields.name: target_character
fields.text: The character the scheme is aimed at.

fields.name: target_title
fields.text: The title the scheme is aimed at.

label: Can start tutorial lesson
summary: Whether the named tutorial lesson can be started.
details: The game's documentation calls it an interface trigger that works only in specific places. Vanilla uses it once, with a lesson name passed in as a parameter.
